findings.title: Ground stop ordered by FAA at all airports in America due to a 'communication issue'
findings.summary_md: The FAA issued an advisory on Friday afternoon, November 13, 2026, ordering a ground stop at all U.S. airports and citing 'extraordinary unforeseen circumstances' for safety. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a nefarious attack and that a telecommunication outage was the cause. Mullin added, 'This isn't another 9/11. There is no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones.'

findings.title: FAA orders nationwide ground stop at all U.S. airports amid 'extraordinary circumstances'
findings.summary_md: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop, directing airports to hold departing traffic due to 'extraordinary circumstances,' according to this local CBS affiliate brief published at 4:15 PM ET on November 13, 2026. The station reported that, per the FAA, all airports in the United States were ground stopped.

findings.title: Live updates on FAA ground stop: No timeline for resolution as flight cancellations climb
findings.summary_md: CNN's live coverage, which began at 4:22 PM ET on November 13, 2026, tracked the nationwide FAA ground stop as flight cancellations climbed. The blog reported no timeline for resolving the stop and showed planes parked on the tarmac at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport.

findings.title: FAA issues nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances,' White House says no indication of 'nefarious act'
findings.summary_md: The White House and the FAA said the issue appeared to be caused by a telecommunication outage, with no indication of a 'nefarious act.' Multiple sources told CBS News that an update to the private communications network connecting America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage; the network is operated by L3Harris. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the grounding was done out of an abundance of caution and that all flights were accounted for.

findings.title: Live Updates: FAA Declares Rare Nationwide Ground Stop of Flights
findings.summary_md: The New York Times live blog, which began at 4:30 PM EST on November 13, 2026, reported that before the nationwide advisory the FAA had already halted flights to Chicago's O'Hare and Midway airports citing equipment problems, and had logged equipment-related departure delays at Newark, Las Vegas, Teterboro, Orlando, Houston and Phoenix. More than 30,000 departures and arrivals were scheduled for the remainder of the day, and the paper noted the stop was only the third nationwide moratorium on flights in recent history, after September 11, 2001, and January 11, 2023.

findings.title: 'This Isn't Another 9/11': FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop 'Due to Extraordinary Circumstances'
findings.summary_md: The FAA halted all departing flights nationwide 'due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,' Gizmodo reported. The outlet noted that CBS News reported around 6:45 PM ET that an update to the private communications network connecting the country's air traffic control system was pushed out on Friday and crashed the system.

findings.title: FAA grounds US flights nationwide after 'communication issue'
findings.summary_md: About 7,000 flights had been delayed or cancelled due to the stop, according to FlightAware, and 4,042 flights were in the air heading to U.S. airports when it was ordered, according to Flightradar24; the communication issue affected all 22 air route traffic control centres. The FAA's post on X described a 'temporary telecommunications outage,' with international flights handled case by case, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication the stop was triggered by a threat. Bloomberg reported the FBI does not believe a cyberattack or criminal activity caused the failure but was examining whether a software update could have. Air Space Intelligence denied that its SMART system, developed under an $875 million contract awarded in June, was responsible, and Senator Tammy Duckworth called for a thorough and complete investigation.
